title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
data_curation: No new training data; the benchmark reuses four agent environments with fixed task sets shared across all methods. ALFWorld: 140 valid_seen games; ScienceWorld: AgentGym split with 2,059 training instances (after removing 61 overlapping task IDs) and 200 evaluation tasks; WebShop: 128 fixed goals; Search-QA: 3,125 questions (500 each from NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue plus all 125 Bamboogle) with top-3 passage retrieval. Rewards are outcome-based: 10 for ALFWorld/WebShop success, 1 for a correct Search-QA answer, ScienceWorld final score / 100, minus an invalid-action penalty (0.1, or 0.01 on Search-QA). Teachers get privileged context from benchmark-specific skill banks (or future observations for OCSD). A side survey counts 47 agentic-distillation arXiv papers in 90 days (25 Jun - 22 Sep 2026), about one every two days.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Every run is a single 100-global-step RL stage from the pretrained Qwen3.5 backbone with no SFT warmup; schedule differences are method-specific, e.g. RLSD's mixing weight decays linearly from 0.5 to 0 over the 100 steps, and OCSD uses a 0.1 warmup ratio on Search-QA. The paper also checks how rankings change at steps 20/40/60/80/100 and within a GRPO-matched training-time budget.
method: An independent benchmark, not a new algorithm: GRPO is compared with ten agentic self-distillation methods, grouped by mechanism. Auxiliary distillation losses: GRPO+OPSD (constant gate), SDAR, Skill-SD, ICSD, PCSD. Advantage reweighting from teacher-student log-prob gaps: RLSD, OCSD, AgentOPSD. Reward shaping: ADRS. Verified teacher continuations with top-32-plus-tail suffix KL: OVCSD. Teachers are the same backbone (pre-update actor, or the frozen reference for PCSD) conditioned on privileged skills; all methods are evaluated without privileged context. The shared setup is full-parameter training in a common text-agent framework: AdamW LR 1e-6, G=8 trajectories per task, PPO clip 0.2 with dual clip 3.0, K3 reference KL 0.01, entropy coefficient 0.001, 512-token turns, temperature 1.0, one node of 8 H800s. Method hyperparameters come from the source papers and released code. In total: 132 runs (11 methods x 4 benchmarks x Qwen3.5-2B/4B/9B), 12,124.4 H800 GPU-hours.
eval_metrics: Final evaluation at T=0.4 over eight rollout seeds (mean +/- SD): ALFWorld success, ScienceWorld task score, Search-QA exact match, WebShop score and success. Training is tracked by validation every 5 steps (2,772 sweeps), normalized validation-curve AUC, peak-to-final drop, and low-performance counts; cost by net training time ratio to GRPO and GPU-hours. Twelve-setting equal-weight means: PCSD 54.26, AgentOPSD 51.34, GRPO 49.68, OCSD 49.50, RLSD 46.54, SDAR 46.33, OVCSD 46.17, ICSD 44.75, ADRS 44.61, GRPO+OPSD 43.05, Skill-SD 39.45. By AUC, OCSD leads (39.88) and AgentOPSD ranks ninth (34.41).
key_results: Only PCSD (+4.58) and AgentOPSD (+1.66) beat GRPO's twelve-setting mean, no method wins across settings, and severe failures occur (e.g. 0.00% WebShop success for Skill-SD and ICSD at 4B and Skill-SD and RLSD at 9B; 1.52% for GRPO+OPSD on 4B ALFWorld). Of 120 method-setting comparisons, 112 cost more training time than GRPO and 58 of those score lower; under a GRPO-matched time budget AgentOPSD's ALFWorld mean falls from 68.10 to 37.63 and PCSD's WebShop mean from 73.17 to 63.83, both below GRPO.
evolution_note: The paper reacts to the 2026 surge of on-policy self-distillation methods for agentic RL (SDAR, Skill-SD, RLSD, OCSD, OVCSD, AgentOPSD, ADRS, ICSD, PCSD), which grew out of OPD/OPSD with privileged-context teachers, and whose papers mostly reuse published baseline numbers. It shifts the emphasis from proposing methods to fair re-evaluation under one protocol. It argues that a well-tuned GRPO remains a strong baseline, and that future work should report repeated evaluation, training-failure analysis, and measured cost together.
